messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: p99 latency spike detected on cont-batch path in us-west2 (alerts: latency-p99 > 1200ms). Auto-paging route: @sam_oncall :rotating_light:

sam_oncall: seeing it, joining. looks like p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.4s for streaming endpoints. any customer-facing errors?

maya_sre: noticed streaming stalls + a few long tail RPCs in the runtime logs. KV cache churn around the same window. linking traces: https://console.redwood/replay/abcd1234 :point_up_2:

leo_infra: confirmed node-level CPU on batchers jumped to 92% on a subset of pods, other pods idle. packing distribution looks skewed (many tiny sequences mixed with some huge sequences).

sam_oncall: TL;DR: mixed-seqlen workload triggered large batches with heterogenous seqs -> long runtime for tails -> scheduling fairness starved streaming lanes. customer impact: some customers saw >2s streaming gaps, 504s rare but reported.

ops-bot: Affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/generate (cont-batch). 34% increase in queued requests for cont-batching pool us-west2.

tess_product: flagged by CS: one customer (alpha-search) reported degraded chat responsiveness and a couple dropped websockets. Need ETA on mitigation.

maya_sre: first mitigation I tried: lowered pack_threshold on cont-batcher from 0.95 -> 0.75 for us-west2-rackA via runtime flag. watch graphs.

sam_oncall: good. also flip preemptive_shed for streaming lanes to enabled (was off for cont-batch for latency reasons). command: 
```
# runtimectl
set runtime.contbatch.pack_threshold=0.75 --scope=us-west2-rackA
set runtime.streaming.preemptive_shed=true --scope=us-west2
```

leo_infra: confirmed flag applied on 6/6 nodes in rackA. immediate effect: p99 dropped from 1.4s -> 820ms over next 2 minutes. p95 steady ~380ms.

sam_oncall: pushing a targeted node drain for a couple of the worst packers to rebalance: `kubectl drain node/pack-uw2-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (will shepherd pods to other machines).

maya_sre: also observed KV eviction spikes; raised kv-cache-size for cont-batch pool by +20% to reduce churn (temp). command: `runtimectl set kv.cache.size=1.2x --pool=contbatch-usw2`.

ops-bot: reminder: enabling preemptive_shed increases early token shedding risk for long-running gen requests. tradeoff accepted to protect streaming SLOs.

tess_product: do we need to proactively notify beta customers? alpha-search still seeing intermittent spacing.

sam_oncall: yes, notify CS with short blurb. severity: SEV-3, partial degradation for some streaming customers; no broad data loss. ETA for stabilization ~ 15-25m with current mitigations.

leo_infra: additional mitigation: changed batcher.max_batch_size from 64 -> 48 for cont-batch pool. This reduces tail amplification from mixing huge sequences. Applied via config rollout to pool with 50% canary first.

maya_sre: canary windows look good; p99 in canary down to 650ms, no errors introduced. scheduling fairness metrics improved (fairness_index +0.12).

sam_oncall: plan: 1) keep pack_threshold=0.75 and preemptive_shed=true for 30m 2) finish rolling batch_size reduction to 48 if canary stable 3) monitor p95/p99 and streaming stalls 4) if not stable, route a portion of high-hetero traffic to dedicated pool (dedicated-usw2-burst) as fallback.

ops-bot: ticket created: INC-1719004327 (cont-batch heterolen p99 spike). paging log: @maya_sre -> acknowledged.

tess_product: CS notified. message sent to customers: "We've identified increased tail latency for streaming in us-west2 and applied mitigations; you may see improved latency in the next 20 minutes. We're monitoring and will follow up."

maya_sre: follow-up checks:
- traces show fewer long-tail KV misses after kv-size bump
- batch size reduction removed a class of 10-20s outliers in internal simulations
- small number of websocket reconnects logged at 1719007000-1719007200 (alpha-search).

sam_oncall: any downstream consequences? memory pressure?

leo_infra: small uptick in GPU memory usage due to slightly more batches but still under threshold. overall cost up ~3% for this pool while mitigations are on.

ops-bot: current SLO numbers: p95=390ms, p99=780ms (prev p99=1400ms). queued requests down to baseline.

sam_oncall: handoff: I'll stay on until p99 stable <800ms for 45m, then hand to @maya_sre for overnight monitoring. add follow-ups: investigate smarter packer heuristics for mixed-seqlen (prefer split by max_seq when variance > X), and add unit test for packaging fairness.

maya_sre: acknowledged. items for next-day: run replayed load tests with synthetic hetero mix (10% > 1024 tokens, 60% < 64) and tune pack_threshold/batch_size automation. create RFC for regional fallback routing policy.

tess_product: noted. I'll coordinate with CS for a postmortem blurb once root cause validated.

sam_oncall: final note: if we see recurrence, escalate to routing engineers to create automatic hot-path diversion to dedicated pools. For now mitigations working, keeping incident open until 1719011200. :white_check_mark:
